title: Rutherford IIb — Immediately Threatened
disclaimer: For professional education and simulation only. Not for direct patient-care decision-making.
synthetic_findings: Sudden severe unilateral lower-limb ischemic pain
Sensory loss extending beyond the toes
Limb salvage depends on immediate revascularization

stages.title: Stage 1: Initial recognition and focused assessment
stages.narrative: A synthetic patient develops sudden severe unilateral limb pain. Focused examination shows sensory loss extending beyond the toes and new mild motor weakness.
stages.question: Which finding most clearly escalates this presentation to an immediately threatened limb?
stages.rationale: Motor weakness is the critical escalation feature separating an immediately threatened Rutherford IIb limb from a marginally threatened IIa limb.
stages.safety_principle: A new motor deficit in acute limb ischemia signals immediate threat and demands immediate vascular-surgery involvement and a reperfusion pathway.

choices.text: New motor weakness accompanying the acute sensory and perfusion abnormalities
choices.feedback: Motor deficit identifies advanced neurological ischemia and the need for immediate escalation.

choices.text: Severe pain alone without considering sensory, motor, or Doppler findings
choices.feedback: Pain is important but does not distinguish IIa from IIb as reliably as the motor examination.

choices.text: A preserved venous Doppler signal, which indicates that the limb is not threatened
choices.feedback: Venous flow may remain audible in IIb and does not negate the neurological evidence of immediate threat.

choices.text: Any sensory symptom, regardless of its distribution or the presence of weakness
choices.feedback: The extent of sensory loss matters, but motor weakness is the defining escalation feature in this synthetic comparison.

stages.title: Stage 2: Rutherford classification
stages.narrative: The synthetic limb has sensory loss beyond the toes, mild-to-moderate motor weakness, no arterial Doppler signal, and a preserved venous Doppler signal.
stages.question: Which Rutherford category best matches these findings?
stages.rationale: Sensory loss beyond the toes plus motor weakness, with absent arterial and preserved venous Doppler signals, defines an immediately threatened Rutherford IIb limb.
stages.safety_principle: Rutherford IIb is salvageable only with immediate revascularization; classification must not introduce delay.

choices.text: Rutherford I — Viable
choices.feedback: A viable limb has no sensory or motor deficit and usually retains audible arterial and venous Doppler signals.

choices.text: Rutherford IIa — Marginally threatened
choices.feedback: Rutherford IIa has no motor weakness and sensory loss is absent or limited to the toes.

choices.text: Rutherford IIb — Immediately threatened
choices.feedback: The extended sensory deficit, motor weakness, and Doppler pattern support Rutherford IIb.

choices.text: Rutherford III — Irreversible
choices.feedback: Rutherford III has profound anesthesia and paralysis, often with absent arterial and venous Doppler signals.

stages.title: Stage 3: Immediate management
stages.narrative: The synthetic limb remains immediately threatened, and no contraindication to anticoagulation has been identified.
stages.question: Which immediate management bundle best matches the urgency of this presentation?
stages.rationale: Immediate vascular-surgery involvement, intravenous unfractionated heparin unless contraindicated, analgesia, resuscitation and supportive care, and repeated neurological and vascular assessment should accompany preparation for immediate reperfusion.
stages.safety_principle: Supportive measures and anticoagulation must occur in parallel with, not instead of, the fastest feasible revascularization pathway.

choices.text: Activate immediate vascular-surgery care, give intravenous unfractionated heparin unless contraindicated, provide resuscitation and analgesia, and repeat limb assessments
choices.feedback: This combines immediate escalation, thrombus-propagation control, supportive care, and surveillance while reperfusion is organized.

choices.text: Observe the motor deficit for several hours before deciding whether specialist involvement is necessary
choices.feedback: Observation risks progression to irreversible ischemia and is incompatible with an immediately threatened limb.

choices.text: Withhold anticoagulation and vascular escalation until a complete elective imaging workup is available
choices.feedback: Imaging must not create harmful delay, and anticoagulation is generally initiated unless contraindicated.

choices.text: Provide analgesia and fluids but defer reperfusion planning until the neurological findings stabilize
choices.feedback: Supportive care is necessary but cannot replace immediate planning for limb-saving reperfusion.

stages.title: Stage 4: Diagnostic imaging and treatment planning
stages.narrative: Immediate reperfusion is being organized. Anatomical imaging may be available without delaying transfer or treatment.
stages.question: How should imaging be used in this Rutherford IIb pathway?
stages.rationale: Anatomical imaging is useful only when it can be obtained immediately, guides the intervention, and does not postpone reperfusion in an immediately threatened limb.
stages.safety_principle: When imaging would delay treatment, the immediate revascularization pathway takes priority over additional anatomical definition.

choices.text: Use immediately available anatomical imaging only if it guides treatment without postponing reperfusion
choices.feedback: This preserves useful anatomical planning while protecting the time-critical reperfusion pathway.

choices.text: Complete a routine sequence of noninvasive and invasive imaging before choosing any treatment
choices.feedback: A routine sequence can create harmful delay in an immediately threatened limb.

choices.text: Observe the limb overnight and obtain elective anatomical imaging if weakness persists
choices.feedback: Motor weakness requires immediate action rather than observation and elective imaging.

choices.text: Avoid imaging in every Rutherford IIb case even when it is immediately available during treatment preparation
choices.feedback: Rapid imaging can guide the fastest suitable intervention when it does not delay reperfusion.

stages.title: Stage 5: Definitive management and escalation
stages.narrative: The synthetic limb remains salvageable but immediately threatened. The vascular team has enough information to choose a reperfusion strategy.
stages.question: Which definitive-management principle is most appropriate?
stages.rationale: Immediate revascularization should use the fastest appropriate surgical, endovascular, catheter-directed, bypass, or hybrid method based on anatomy, etiology, symptom duration, severity, bleeding risk, comorbidity, available expertise, and time to reperfusion.
stages.safety_principle: No single technique is universally correct, but any avoidable delay threatens progression from salvageable IIb ischemia to irreversible tissue injury.

choices.text: Proceed immediately with the fastest suitable revascularization method selected for anatomy, cause, duration, severity, bleeding risk, comorbidity, expertise, and time to flow restoration
choices.feedback: This prioritizes immediate reperfusion while recognizing that technique selection is individualized.

choices.text: Use open surgical thromboembolectomy for every Rutherford IIb limb regardless of anatomy or etiology
choices.feedback: Open thromboembolectomy may be appropriate, but no technique is universal across all lesions and causes.

choices.text: Schedule catheter-directed thrombolysis electively after a period of observation for neurological improvement
choices.feedback: Elective delay is unsafe; catheter-directed therapy is only one possible immediate strategy in selected anatomy and risk profiles.

choices.text: Continue anticoagulation and supportive care alone while waiting for motor weakness to resolve
choices.feedback: Medical therapy alone does not provide the immediate reperfusion required by a salvageable Rutherford IIb limb.
